Hi Taylor — great questions. Short answers up front, then a suggested next step and an attached one-pager you can share with procurement/legal.

Quick summary:
- Marketplace (public listing): Fast procurement path, consolidated billing through AWS, often simpler PO routing. Limited flexibility on negotiated terms — most standard marketplace listings use the marketplace flow and terms.
- Private Offer on a marketplace: Marketplace billing but allows custom pricing, extended payment terms, and a private-offer MSA overlay (recommended when you need negotiated commercial/term flexibility while keeping marketplace billing).
- Direct Redwood contract (invoice/MSA): Full contract flexibility, can include stricter SLAs, data residency clauses, SOC 2 + KMS/HSM language. Typically required for complex regulatory requirements or when you need bespoke indemnities.

Co-sell / credits:
- If you want AWS co-sell credit recognition, a Private Offer is the most straightforward; public listing can also qualify but the AWS GTM/partner motion usually prefers Private Offers so the AWS team can attribute referrals and pipeline. I'll loop in Ben (our AE) and Laura (partner ops) for precise credit mechanics.

Recommendation for Novus Health (healthcare/regulatory):
- If you need explicit contract language for data residency and indemnities, go direct OR Private Offer + Redwood-managed MSA. If your procurement team strongly prefers marketplace invoice paths (SAP integrations), Private Offer hits the middle ground.

Next steps:
1) I attached a one-pager comparing the two paths (redwood_marketplace_vs_direct_onepager.pdf).
2) Ben will follow up with the AWS co-sell mechanics and typical timelines.
3) If you want, we can draft a Private Offer term sheet and route it through AWS/your procurement; that usually takes 7–14 business days for approvals.

Available for a 30-min call on Thu or Fri morning PST — let me know what works.

Hi Taylor — looping in details you can take to finance/procurement.

Co-sell/credits:
- Private Offer is preferred for co-sell attribution because the AWS account team can log the opportunity against the private-offer offer id; that makes it easy to attribute pipeline and credits. Public listings can be credited but require additional coordination and sometimes rely on downstream attribution via invoice records (less reliable).

Payment terms:
- Private Offer can be configured to support longer payment terms (e.g., 45–60 days) depending on AWS marketplace policy and Redwood acceptance. We frequently use Private Offers to accommodate SAP/PO flows while preserving co-sell. If you need 60 days, we can propose that in the Private Offer term sheet.

Security/evidence timeline: 
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and our security addendum are standard; we can provide an auditor package within 3–5 business days after a signed NDA/LOE. For direct contracts the contractual security addendum is straightforward; for Private Offer we attach the same security docs and can add explicit language referencing SOC 2/KMS controls.

Recommended path for Novus (healthcare + SAP-driven procurement):
1) Create Private Offer with 45–60 day payment terms to match your PO cycle. This preserves marketplace billing and allows the AWS team to co-sell.
2) Attach our standard security addendum and provide the SOC 2 package once we have an NDA.
3) If you need specific indemnity/residency clauses beyond our standard addendum, we can either (a) layer a Redwood MSA over the Private Offer or (b) go direct for full negotiation.

I attached a procurement checklist (novus_procurement_checklist.xlsx) to help your ops team map internal systems. Also created a draft HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/ND-20261207-NOVUS (internal).
